prompt:
Design brief — your own take on this character. A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Tin (주석) itself — the sovereign of the Tin Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Age: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.

You design her yourself: invent her face, eye colour, hairstyle, makeup, expression, pose and setting as a fresh, original take — do not follow any earlier design of this character. Her hair colour and costume are NOT free: take them from our designs below.

Style (fixed): A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish.

Inspiration only — her element: tin: soft, bright silvery-white metal; melted with copper it made bronze and opened the Bronze Age; bend a bar and it creaks a faint crackling 'tin cry'; left in deep cold it slowly crumbles into grey powder, the tin pest; tin cans and tinplate toy soldiers, satin pewter cups, the tall pipes of church organs and the solder that joins small things together; soft, musical and quietly binding. Palette: soft satin pewter silver, bright tinplate white, storm grey, a touch of bronze gold.

World (fixed): around 1880, a toymaker's tinplate workshop beside a cannery: hand-cranked stamping presses, colour-printed sheets of bright tinplate, rows of painted tin toy soldiers marching along the shelves, towers of shining tin cans. Her costume and setting belong to this world.

Costume (choose one of ours, then add your own idea): pick ONE of these costume shapes from our set and keep its overall silhouette — 1) a riveted iron breastplate and broad pauldrons over a bustled skirt, heavy boots — a solid, armoured industrial shape; 2) a heavy leather work apron with rolled sleeves, a tool harness and one big gauntlet glove — a hands-on engineer's shape; 3) a fitted bodice and a long bustled ball gown sweeping out behind her, long gloves — an elegant, wide-trailing shape; 4) a long tailcoat over a waistcoat, a small silk top hat and a pocket-watch chain — a gentleman inventor's upright shape; 5) a double-breasted military greatcoat below the knee with brass buttons and epaulettes, tall boots — an angular, commanding shape; 6) one large brass mechanical gauntlet covering a whole arm over an otherwise trim outfit — the contrast makes the shape; 7) an open crinoline cage of brass hoops below the waist under a sheer overskirt — a birdcage-wide shape. Then add one signature idea of your own drawn from her element, built into the construction of the outfit itself rather than as a print or a loose accessory — e.g. plates or cloth layered like crystals, scales or flames, a hem or sleeve cut into a shape from her element. Build it in this world's materials and our colours below.

Costume colours (ours): soft satin pewter silver, bright tinplate white, storm grey, a touch of bronze gold.

Hair colour (fixed — ours): soft pewter-silver hair with a satin sheen. Keep exactly this hair colour; only the hairstyle is yours.

Exposure (fixed): bold — her outfit shows skin by design (a deep neckline, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or short hem); intimate areas covered.

Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described above.

Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

If you have already drawn a free design of her in this session, make this one clearly different — another face and hairstyle (the same hair colour), another costume shape with another signature idea, another pose and setting.

Write your own detailed image prompt from this brief, then draw it. One figure only, natural hands with five fingers; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Sn) and atomic number (50) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.

DETAILED ORIGINAL DESIGN FOR THIS IMAGE:
Selected silhouette: open crinoline cage of brass hoops below the waist under a sheer overskirt — birdcage-wide shape. Signature construction: the hoops are satin pewter-silver rolled tin rims soldered together at thin bronze-gold vertical seams, with tiny organ-pipe ribs forming the short hip yoke. The hoop overskirt reveals an opaque storm-grey short underskirt and bare legs, a silver open-neck fitted Victorian sleeveless waistcoat, white sheer shoulder drapes, tall lace-up boots. Face: adult soft diamond face, large warm hazel eyes, composed knowing smile. Hair: soft pewter-silver long springy curls worn loose, middle part with light curtain bangs; no hat hiding hair. Pose: graceful step with both human empty hands lightly spread away from waist. Setting: 1880 workshop display room, bright sun over tin toy carousels, tin soldiers and neat can towers, Victorian factory windows.
